LESSON: ACTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Active Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Active Listening, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: What are the strategies of active listening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch an audio-visual recording about animals and birds,

2. work jointly to identify the animals and birds from the recording,

3. list the vocabulary on flashcards and organise in a class portfolio,

4. collaborate with peers to describe the animals based on their colour and size,

5. team up with peers to prepare a mosaic of a farm animal of choice,

6. display the mosaic during the art exhibition and interclass contests.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch an audio-visual recording about animals and birds,
2. work jointly to identify the animals and birds from the recording,
3. list the vocabulary on flashcards and organise in a class portfolio,
4. collaborate with peers to describe the animals based on their colour and size,
5. team up with peers to prepare a mosaic of a farm animal of choice,
6. display the mosaic during the art exhibition and interclass contests.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Active Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively to work jointly to identify the animals

and birds from the recording.

• Self-efficacy: This is portrayed as the learner shows defining personal skills when describing the animals based on their

colour and size.

6

Values:
Respect: This is nurtured as the learner appreciates diverse opinions while describing the animals based on their colour and

size.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Animal welfare: This is promoted as the learner identifies and describes various animals found in their locality.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate this concept about animals and birds to similar concepts as covered in Agriculture.
